meaning.evidence: Every fact kept: Tuesday night, the ads for couples, the book of dances, twenty-one quadrilles to four, Mellie Dunham's change of plans, Tex Rickard and Madison Square Garden.

sense.evidence: Mostly exact ("big crack at", "put the word out in the papers", "the Tuesday night do", "his missus"), but "Mr. Ford fired up" reads as got angry rather than exclaimed.

authenticity.evidence: Natural on the whole ("chipping in a few old-time tunes", "standardise the bloody things"), with US "folks" left.

register.evidence: A clear Aussie retelling but closer to level 3 than a level-5 yarn; much is light paraphrase ("It was also said that putting on this dance was meant to help Henry Ford's push"). Swearing within level 2.

tone.evidence: Keeps the light news item, told conversationally ("Right, so Henry Ford's first big crack").

flow.evidence: Long, over-packed sentence for Mellie Dunham ("chipping in a few old-time tunes for the Ford 'Americana' collection of those pieces that's being got ready for publishing").

essence.evidence: Plainly the AP item about Ford's square-dance campaign.

A.summary: Accurate and readable, but pitched lighter than the level-5 brief.

meaning.evidence: "he'll be crook management of Tex Rickard" garbles who will manage him, and "Dec. Crikey, 13" breaks the dateline; the rest is the original verbatim.

sense.evidence: "crook management" (crook = sick or dodgy), "Far out, but plans were changed", "front up" barely fits.

authenticity.evidence: Stage-Australian bolt-ons: "Crikey", "Bloody hell", "Fair fuckin' dinkum", "Oh, shit", "Streeeeewth."

register.evidence: Exclamations sprinkled on untranslated news prose ("to form a nucleus for the party"); swearing within level 2 but no real retelling.

tone.evidence: Ford's quote and the news item become random cursing: "Fair fuckin' dinkum, what we're tryin' to do".

essence.evidence: The item is there underneath but buried in noise.

B.summary: Rule-engine noise on an untranslated item, with a garbled key fact.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept; additions hang off the original: "so the rest have someone to follow" explains nucleus, "Twenty-one down to four." reacts to the selection, "Not bad for a grandpa with a fiddle, ay?" reacts to the vaudeville offer.

sense.evidence: Exact: "gettin' 'em all done the same way" for standardize, "whacked an ad in the paper", "the Tuesday night do", "front up".

authenticity.evidence: A natural yarn voice ("got it into his noggin", "quick as a whip", "shindig"), with US "folks" and "ay?" for eh.

register.evidence: A full level-5 retelling of every paragraph; swearing light ("that bloody great shindig"), inside level 2.

tone.evidence: Keeps the light, slightly amused news story, now as a yarn.

flow.evidence: Reads naturally aloud: "Story goes, Henry Ford, the motor car bloke, has got it into his noggin".

variety.evidence: Varied throughout: "crack at it", "scrapin' away", "bright lights", "shindig".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the Ford square-dance story, retold.

C.summary: A lively, faithful level-5 yarn with apt asides.
